1265278875568730114 [2020-05-26] @visakanv 💜 296 🔁 39 [(SEED) type=root]
I say this with love, and as someone on the path myself: I think choosing to become a public figure is a sort of voluntary descent into a kind of madness. I think it's a psychological extreme sport with very high odds of injury
├── 1265303155438284800 [2020-05-26] @patio11 💜 34
│   @visakanv I have heard a lot of people say this but, as a data point, would not put this in my top 10 challenges in life at any point through the present.
│   ├── 1265303529259823106 [2020-05-26] @patio11 💜 10
│   │   @visakanv Like, is it harder psychologically than getting married or parenting? Because while there is a wide spectrum of experiences for both, the happy case is culturally normative and a lot harder of an ongoing commitment than working in public, along many axes.
│   └── 1265304018521210880 [2020-05-26] @visakanv 💜 6
│       @patio11 I think we are similar in that we are uncommonly well-suited to it. I wouldn’t list it in my top 5, not sure about 10 but probably not that either. I do also find that I’ve done a lot of reading, thinking and simulating that others haven’t
├── 1265431662801965056 [2020-05-26] @michelleakin 💜 1
│   @visakanv Yep yep yep yep yep
└── 1265433750562672641 [2020-05-27] @CountJ0ecool 💜 1
    @visakanv I'd say the same about game development, or probably any creative endeavor. Never start. (And back to game development for me)

===

1265581187210280961 [2020-05-27] @m_ashcroft 💜 27 🔁 1
Me: Number of followers is a vanity metric and a distraction. What really matters is the quality of conversations and relationships that I cultivate. 🧘‍♂️

Also me: Let's see if I can get to 2,000 by the end of May lol 🤪
↓
1265596763592941569 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 1
@m_ashcroft Follower count is a good metric, actually. It represents potential that you can drop upon.
↓
1265596924683595778 [2020-05-27] @m_ashcroft 
@DRMacIver Can you rephrase "potential you can drop upon"? I am not grokking.
↓
1265597087418396672 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 1
@m_ashcroft err. "draw upon". Accidental wrong word.
↓
1265597374543642625 [2020-05-27] @m_ashcroft 
@DRMacIver Gotcha. 

I mean, yes. I'd rather 500 engaged,. interesting, curious people I talk to than 10k bots though, which is more what I was pointing at.
↓
1265597888941490177 [2020-05-27] @m_ashcroft 💜 1
@DRMacIver Of course I'd rather have 10k engaged, interesting, curious people than 500 as well, so...
↓
1265598474084585472 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 2
@m_ashcroft Yeah I think basically it's a good metric in the presence of careful curation and not doing stupid number-gaming things, and Twitter is bad anyway if you're doing the latter.
↓
1265598687415279616 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 2 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
@m_ashcroft But of course eventually you run into this problem. https://t.co/kg7U8T5gzQ
  [Quoting @visakanv: I say this with love, and as someone on the path myself: I think choosing to become a public figure is a sort of voluntary descent into a kind of madness. I think it's a psychological extreme sport with very high odds of injury]

1265602781680992257 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 30 🔁 4 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
One of the weirdest things about Twitter is that it basically puts us all on this path. It's no longer a question of "Are you a public figure?" but "How public a figure are you?"

I don't think people realise how much of a psychological shift this is because it happens gradually. https://t.co/kg7U8T5gzQ
  [Quoting @visakanv: I say this with love, and as someone on the path myself: I think choosing to become a public figure is a sort of voluntary descent into a kind of madness. I think it's a psychological extreme sport with very high odds of injury]
├── 1265603110199648256 [2020-05-27] @visakanv 💜 2
│   @DRMacIver yup. and if you don't prepare for it advance, it'll likely catch you off guard
│   ↓
│   1265605705760940033 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 4
│   @visakanv Yeah. I'm lucky in that I've mostly done slow burn growth - new followers trickle in, but there have no been big spikes, so once I noticed this was happening I had plenty of adjustment time to figure out how to set good boundaries with the larger numbers.
│   ├── 1265605850414055426 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 2
│   │   @visakanv It's still a bit weird though and sometimes requires me to experiment in other forums and forms in order to find new ways of being that I can then backport into my public presence.
│   └── 1265605880969482244 [2020-05-27] @visakanv 
│       @DRMacIver 💪🏾 best way to grow!
│       ↓
│       1265607915253182464 [2020-05-27] @m_ashcroft 💜 2
│       @visakanv @DRMacIver I feel like the same is happening for me, though I have no benchmarks. Is 4x growth from 500 to 2000 in 6 months slow growth? No idea.
│       
│       But I do notice subtle shifts in 'vibe' after some implicit thresholds are passed and I need to readjust each time.
│       ↓
│       1265627582575280129 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 2
│       @m_ashcroft @visakanv That feels like reasonably fast growth to me. Certainly it's a lot faster than mine - I'm not sure offhand when I passed the 2000 mark but a couple years ago certainly.
└── 1265603449925914625 [2020-05-27] @DRMacIver 💜 5
    Locked accounts are an exception obviously
